summary: Discovery with Ironclad Security on on-prem / air-gapped options. Customer is highly regulated, requires fully air-gapped deployment with offline update procedures, HSM integration, and strict patching windows. Discussed Redwood Private architecture, offline model/package signing, PKI-based update distribution, hardware choices, and tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Private. Agreed next steps to exchange security docs and schedule a security deep dive.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE) -- Mark Reynolds (Ironclad Head of Infra), Aisha Khan (Ironclad CISO), Tom Wu (DevOps), Sofia Delgado (Compliance)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. we're gonna, um, do a quick intro, run through your environment and the constraints for on-prem / air gapped deployments, and then Priya will go into architecture.
00:12 Mark Reynolds: Thanks, Jordan. quick note, we are under a code-name project vault, so prefer minimal distribution. we can't do any external internet egress from the inference cluster.
00:20 Jordan Lee: Got it — fully air-gapped. Aisha, anything from compliance side to state up front?
00:24 Aisha Khan: Yeah, SOC2 is table stakes for us, but more importantly we need HSM-backed key management, FIPS-validated crypto for model keys, and we have to demonstrate an offline update process that leaves an audit trail. also need RBAC and strong SSO — we use Okta.
00:37 Priya Kapoor: Okay that tracks. Redwood Private supports a private control plane that can be run in your VPC or completely on-prem with no outbound. for fully air-gapped we provide an appliance-style bundle plus update artifacts that you float in via your secure media process.
00:50 Tom Wu: How do updates work? like, we have weekly patch windows but for model updates we prefer quarterly sign-off. do you do signed model artifacts?
00:58 Miguel Santos: yes — we sign model artifacts with our build key; for air-gapped installs we can provide signed bundles and a verification step using your PKI. you can also re-sign or verify using your HSM; we provide tooling to validate signatures before installing.
01:10 Mark Reynolds: And what about telemetry? we can't have external telemetry leaving that network.
01:15 Jordan Lee: By default we can disable all telemetry and any usage data can be written to a local logstore. we have an offline diagnostics bundle you can upload to support, or if you prefer we can run a support session where you paste logs into a temporary upload portal behind a jump-host.
01:32 Aisha Khan: We need audit logs immutable for six months, and the logs may need to be copied to our SIEM in the segmented network. is that possible?
01:39 Priya Kapoor: yes, we can configure log sinks to local syslog or to your on-prem Splunk/ELK. we also support signed log rotation and can output in RFC5424 format for ingestion.
01:49 Tom Wu: Hardware — our datacenter currently runs mostly A100s but we're evaluating H100 and some L40s for cost. any recommendations?
01:56 Priya Kapoor: H100s give best perf for fp16/bf16 large-context models; A100s are still solid for many models. L40s are a lower-cost option for smaller embeddings or trimmed models. also quan — if you plan to run int8 or 4-bit quantized models we can recommend kernel profiles. we'll include a TCO sheet comparing throughput and cost between A100/H100 and impact on latency.
02:14 Mark Reynolds: Do you support running the control plane air-gapped or does Redwood need connectivity for licensing?
02:19 Jordan Lee: For air-gapped we offer two options: 1) private control plane fully on-prem with license tokens distributed via signed packages, or 2) a hybrid where the control plane is offline but a license server on your network validates signatures locally. no outbound required in both cases.
02:35 Sofia Delgado: Are there any third-party dependencies that call home? we have very strict vendor requirements.
02:40 Miguel Santos: No external calls by default in the air-gapped bundle. the installer will check only local components. optional components like model catalog updates or telemetry are disabled. any 3rd party libs are vetted and included in the SBOM we provide.
02:53 Aisha Khan: KMS integration — we use Thales HSM on-prem. do you have integrations or patterns?
02:58 Priya Kapoor: we integrate with KMIP-compatible HSMs and can also support PKCS#11. for HSM-backed key wrapping of model artifacts we can show an architecture where the signing key is stored in your HSM and Redwood's package verify process uses your public key.
03:15 Mark Reynolds: For vulnerability management, we have quarterly patch windows and can't reboot production during day hours; how are runtime updates handled?
03:22 Miguel Santos: We support node-level canary rolling upgrades; for model updates it's just replacing artifacts and warming KV caches. we can do zero-downtime rollout by spinning new serving pods in a segregated subnet and gradually shifting traffic. all of this can be orchestrated through your private control plane.
03:40 Tom Wu: Do you support offline model provenance? we need chain-of-custody for every model and prompt set used for regulated inferences.
03:45 Priya Kapoor: yes — we keep a provenance record for each model: build hash, signer, artifact manifest, and optional training metadata. those manifests are included in the signed bundle and stored in local artifact store. you can export for audits.
03:56 Mark Reynolds: latency expectations — we need sub-100ms p95 for short prompts under 256 tokens for certain services. can you reach that on-prem?
04:04 Priya Kapoor: depends on hardware and batch sizing; with H100 and optimized kernels we have customers hitting 40–70ms p95 for smaller context models. A100 may be closer to 80–120ms depending on model and quantization. we'll include benchmark samples; also note that caching and local prefix cache reduces repeated costs.
04:25 Aisha Khan: Who owns the data at rest encryption keys? we can't have vendor-controlled keys.
04:30 Jordan Lee: you own them — Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) and we integrate with your KMS or HSM. for Private installs keys never leave your boundary unless you opt-in.
04:38 Mark Reynolds: about licensing — what's the model for private? flat fee, per-GPU, or hybrid?
04:44 Jordan Lee: we do a couple of things — a platform license plus capacity commits (per-GPU) for Dedicated. for on-prem fully private we propose a subscription with a baseline platform fee and optional committed GPU bundles. we'll detail options in the pricing sheet.
04:56 Tom Wu: does Redwood support air-gapped model training or only inference?
04:59 Priya Kapoor: primarily inference. we can ingest locally trained models as signed artifacts. training pipelines remain with you or a separate managed partner.
05:07 Sofia Delgado: audit — do you provide ready artifacts for auditors?
05:10 Miguel Santos: yes, we can provide SBOMs, signed manifests, operational runbook, and the change logs. plus we can provide sample statements for SOC2/ISO controls we've already mapped.
05:22 Mark Reynolds: performance isolation — will noisy tenants impact p95? we are planning to multi-tenant per team but want strict limits.
05:29 Priya Kapoor: we support GPU partitioning and cgroup-level limits; with Dedicated pools you get reserved queues to guarantee throughput. we can also carve capacity by model route.
05:40 Aisha Khan: network segmentation — we need egress filters and strict ACLs.
05:44 Jordan Lee: supported. firewall rules can be enforced and the installer doesn't require opening outbound ports.
05:48 Mark Reynolds: any gotchas for air-gapped: firmware updates, vendor drivers?
05:51 Miguel Santos: yes, firmware/driver updates are your responsibility; we recommend a validated baseline image (OS + driver versions) and we'll certify Redwood runtime against that baseline. we provide compatibility matrix.
06:05 Tom Wu: Ok, thinking about proof-of-concept: we'd like a small pilot on two A100 nodes, no internet, using a medium-size LLM for our internal QA assistant. timeline is 6–8 weeks.
06:14 Jordan Lee: that sounds reasonable for a POC — typical steps: sign NDA, exchange security docs, provide install media, Redwood provides on-site or remote install and runbench. Priya can run a benchmark script and collect results.
06:26 Priya Kapoor: we'll need a person on your side with SRE access to install and witness the rollout. also we need your server model and root certs for PKI validation.
06:35 Mark Reynolds: Budget — we have pre-allocated funds for infrastructure but licensing needs to be approvable by procurement in Jan. any expedited procurement paths?
06:43 Jordan Lee: we can provide an initial POC quote and a smaller pilot pricing that can be mid-year capitalized. procurement usually wants an SOW — we'll include standard terms and an on-prem addendum.
06:53 Aisha Khan: last Q: can you run model explainability/risk tooling on-prem? we need redaction and PII detection pre-output.
06:59 Priya Kapoor: we provide inference hooks for pre- and post-processing so you can run redaction inline. we can also ship rules for PII detection and a local policy engine if needed.
07:12 Mark Reynolds: great. any competitors you think we should be aware of?
07:16 Jordan Lee: a few — Anthropic and OpenAI mostly for hosted, some customers build private stacks themselves or use cloud vendor managed endpoints; we can map differences in controls.
07:25 Sofia Delgado: ok let's recap next steps.
07:28 Jordan Lee: recap: Jordan to send SOC2 + on-prem architecture and runbook; Priya to send TCO + benchmark examples and pilot plan; customer to share server inventory, root CA certs, and list of stakeholders; schedule security deep dive for week of Jan 11th.
07:46 Mark Reynolds: perfect. thanks everyone.
07:49 Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and the docs.
07:52 (call ends)

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-heard words and run-ons as typical. Customers emphasized: offline update signing, HSM integration, no telemetry, SBOM, and audit exports. POC requested on two A100 nodes, timeline 6-8 weeks.
